messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: iAns error
parts:
Thanks John.
The problem is not jumping out at me, so let me suggest some strategies (and/or you can send the data off-list, as you mentioned).
I suspect you're right the issue is in BUGS_modelDef.R.  Some of the code there constructs chunks of R code and then evaluates them to extract information about for loops and sometimes constants.  The error looks like it involves some of that constructed code.
The first thing I would try is to use 'calculate=FALSE' to confirm the error still occurs, which means it has to do with processing the model code to determine the DAG structure (which I think is the case), as opposed to running the custom functions.
Next I would try, to the extent possible, cutting out portions of the model (or, sometimes easier, building up the model from scratch component by component), to narrow down what component introduces the error.
Also I would triple-check that your constants are populated with valid values of correct sizes.  (In the code you sent, Consts$n and Consts$m have not been set, but I'm guessing that was an oversight in putting together the code to send, because you would have hit an error otherwise from that. Or maybe I missed it.)
And I would start poking most at the code with the for loop with 'i' as the indexing variable.  You could even just change that variable name and see if the variable in the error message changes to match.  That would confirm that some code in that loop is the issue.  Now I'm starting to speculate.
And if you're really adventurous, you could set "options(error = recover)" and then when thrown into a browser you will likely be in the source code function "expandContextAndReplacements" (where "context" here refers to the for-loops in which a line of code occurs).  If you open that up, you can see variables to inspect and they might contain clues.  Then you'd be pretty deep into things but that might be of interest to you.
Again, feel free to send the data and reproducible code off-list.
HTH
Perry

messages.author: 8ea376409c2832ae
messages.subject: Re: iAns error
parts:
Thanks, Perry! In case this helps anybody else, the culprit was actually a very silly error (indexing a multivariate node from [i:constant] vs [1:constant], where constant =75, and where i was not defined as a constant or loop index). So it seems that "Error in i[iAns]:75 : NA/NaN" roughly means that the indexing lacked any definition.

John
